Subject: Sealed environment: offline package acceptance & handoff plan

Hi team —

Following our call last week, attaching a draft plan for handing off an offline signed bundle to Island Biotech's sealed cluster (their on-prem DC). High level asks:

- We need a concrete acceptance checklist for Island's ops team that they can run without outbound connectivity.
- Confirm the signing format we will use (detached signature, timestamping, cert chain) and the verification steps that Atlas will provide on handoff.
- Agree on a 3-day install window (target week of Apr 23) and a rollback window/criteria.

Attachments: draft-offline-manifest-v1.json (contains the bundle manifest and SBOM mapping) and handoff-checklist-draft.pdf.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Atlas to confirm sig/hash algorithm and provide sample verification workflow.
2) Island to confirm install window and courier acceptance policy.
3) Redwood to provide signed key certificate and custody form at handoff.

Please reply with any blockers by EOD Wed so we can lock the window.

Thanks,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Program Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Sealed environment: offline package acceptance & handoff plan

Dylan / Island Ops —

Thanks for the plan. A few clarifying items from Atlas Sec before we sign off:

- Verification primitives: we prefer a detached signature + RFC 3161 timestamping. Hashing: SHA-256 for payloads, signatures over manifest using RSA-PSS (4096) or ECDSA P-384 depending on regulatory constraints. Is Redwood ok with RSA-PSS 4096 as the canonical path?
- Key custody: who is the organizational owner of the signing key? We need the cert chain and a signed statement of key rotation policy (retain last two rotation epochs).
- Offline verification doc: we will produce two artifacts — a one-page quick-check for Island on a USB stick and a longer verification script for their SOC engineer. Confirm that both are acceptable.
- Courier: do you require a tamper-evident seal procedure and two-person witness at Redwood pick-up? We can coordinate a vetted courier list.

I'll attach Atlas's compliance questions (short form) — please fill and return; it helps speed internal approvals.

Regards,
Ravi Kapoor
Operations Lead — Atlas Sec
atlas-sec@secureops.com

Attachments: atlas-compliance-questions.docx

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Atlas Sec <atlas-sec@secureops.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Island Biotech <ops@islandbio.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sealed environment: offline package acceptance & handoff plan

Ravi / team —

Short answers inline:

- Signing: RSA-PSS (4096) + SHA-256 is acceptable as primary. We will also include an ECDSA P-384 signature for teams that prefer ECC verification. The bundle will include detached sigs in the standard .sig form and an accompanying "manifest.sigmeta" file listing the cert serials and timestamp token.

- Key custody: Redwood will act as the issuer for this release. The signing key is held in an HSM-backed KMS (Redwood custody) with key splitting for emergency operations. We will produce a signed statement (pdf) describing the rotation cadence (annual rotation, emergency rotation policy included). The actual key material will never leave Redwood HSM; we will export only public certs.

- Offline verification artifacts: we will provide the one-page quick-check and a verification script that runs locally (no internet) — it verifies sha256 sums against the manifest and validates the detached signature against the provided cert chain. Both will be on the signed USB bundle.

- Timestamping: we will include an RFC3161 timestamp token embedded in the signature metadata. If Island's operators require an independent time-stamp check we will annotate the expected signer timestamp in the manifest.

- Rollback plan: acceptance tests (pre-install checklist) + smoke tests post-install. If smoke tests fail, we will revert to previous image via the onboard image rollback that Island already has configured. The manual rollback window is 4 hours; automated cutover rollback criteria included in the checklist.

I'll attach the signing cert we will publish (signed-key-cert.pem) and an updated handoff checklist PDF with the rollback criteria filled in. Please review and call out any additions.

-Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Lead, Private Deployments Security
Redwood Inference

All —

I reviewed the checklist and the certificate. From a compliance/GRC perspective this meets our baseline for sealed deliveries. Two small asks before final:
1) Add a field in the manifest for "custody_witness_names" (printed names of the two Redwood witnesses at handoff).
2) Include a redwood-approved courier name from our vendor list (we cannot accept unknown couriers without a procurement exception).

If those are added, I approve moving forward with the Apr 23 window. I'll trigger DocuSign for the custody statement today and loop procurement for courier approval.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Director, Security & GRC

- Island: please confirm the Apr 23 02:00–06:00 install window (PST) and provide contact for the on-site custodian who will sign custody forms upon receipt.
- Marissa: awaiting the DocuSign custody statement and courier approval list.
- Karthik / Hannah: finalize the manifest with the custody_witness_names field and embed the timestamp token reference. Upload the final bundle and manifest to Drive and paste the link here when ready.

I'll coordinate pickup with Atlas once procurement confirms the courier. Please treat this as high priority — isolated deployments are a common escalation vector and we want the runbook to be frictionless for Island's ops team.

Thanks,
Dylan
